name: Chip supply
summary: China extends its pause on expanded rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan; no TSMC or Samsung stoppage found
state: China's commerce ministry said on 9 Nov it will keep its expanded critical-mineral export controls suspended for two more months, formalising the US–China truce extension to 10 Jan (The National). Licensing controls on seven medium and heavy rare earths from April 2025 remain, and TSMC has asked suppliers for equipment motors without Chinese rare-earth magnets (Tom's Hardware, 22 Oct). Taiwan is weighing tighter chip export controls to mainland China (Caixin, 5 Nov). No TSMC or Samsung output stoppage was found.
for_you: Chip supply is not disrupted. Manufacturers that rely on rare-earth magnets remain exposed to Chinese licensing decisions, now deferred to January.
rubric_hit: Export controls in force on key inputs (China rare-earth licences); no major TSMC/Samsung disruption

sources.title: The National — China extends pause on rare earth export curbs for two months
Tom's Hardware — TSMC is seeking chipmaking equipment that doesn't contain Chinese rare-earth magnets
Caixin Global — Taiwan weighs tighter controls on chip exports to Chinese mainland

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
